claims.text: Equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi can exist as a homogeneous, single-phase simple solid solution.
The simple-solid-solution CoCrFeNiTi starting state has a uniform elemental distribution.
The simple-solid-solution CoCrFeNiTi starting state has favorable plasticity.
The simple-solid-solution CoCrFeNiTi starting state has favorable machinability.
The simple-solid-solution CoCrFeNiTi starting state has relatively low hardness.
The simple-solid-solution CoCrFeNiTi starting state has relatively low strength.
Extensive dynamic recovery governs the relatively low hardness and strength of this alloy state.
The homogeneous, high-symmetry simple-solid-solution structure enables extensive dynamic recovery.
Dynamic recovery minimizes dislocation accumulation.
Reduced dislocation accumulation limits work hardening.
The homogeneous, high-symmetry structure facilitates easy dislocation motion.
Recovery proceeds through dislocation rearrangement or annihilation under mechanical loading.
Heat-treatment-induced nanoscale precipitates impede dynamic recovery by pinning dislocations.
Impeded recovery in the precipitate-modified state increases dislocation storage.
The precipitate-modified state will have higher yield strength than the simple-solid-solution state.
The precipitate-modified state will have higher hardness than the simple-solid-solution state.
The precipitate-modified state will have a higher work-hardening rate than the simple-solid-solution state.
The precipitate-modified state will have a higher dislocation density than the simple-solid-solution state.
The simple-solid-solution state will exhibit more prominent subgrain or recovery structures than the precipitate-modified state.
The proposed mechanism applies at room temperature and moderate strain rates to equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
